messages:
support_ryan: Heads up — customer ACME (acct 123456789012) is seeing intermittent KMS Decrypt failures (AccessDenied) starting ~2026-02-28 03:12 UTC and, weirdly, there are no corresponding KMS/CloudTrail Decrypt events in their org trail for the failing requests. I have a sample SDK error and request IDs below. Any ideas?

eng_security_alex: Can you paste one of the full request IDs, region, and whether the calls are cross-account or using a assume-role? Also did they rotate the CMK or swap aliases recently?

support_ryan: sample request IDs: 
```
requestId: 9a1b2c3d-4567-890a-bcde-1234567890ab
requestId: 7c8d9e0f-1122-3344-5566-77889900aabb
```
Region: eu-west-1.
They do use a cross-account role (platform -> customer). We did an alias swap earlier that morning (alias/redwood/acme-cmk -> new key id). SDK: aws-sdk-js v3.4. Decrypt call includes encryptionContext: { "customerId": "acme" }.

infra_jess: Quick checks: CloudTrail always records KMS API calls, but if CloudTrail delivery to S3 is failing (PutObject denied) you can see gaps. Also if the deny happens before KMS (e.g., AssumeRole/STS permission denied) you'll see STS events but not KMS. Did they change the org S3 bucket policy or enable block-public-access tweaks?

customer_success_maya: Customer timeline: errors spike right after the alias swap at 03:15 UTC. They also noticed a billing blip (lots of retries). They didn't touch CloudTrail config. They did have a security tweak rolled out to S3 bucket policies earlier that window.

eng_security_alex: Hypothesis: alias swap created a new CMK that doesn't have the same grants/policy and the cross-account role lacks kms:Decrypt on the new key. Mixed behavior explained by cached long-lived creds — some requests hit old key/temporary cached grants and succeeded, others hit new key and failed. Two reasons logs might be missing: 1) CloudTrail S3 delivery errors, 2) requests never reached KMS because of an IAM/STSPolicy boundary that blocked the call earlier. Steps to repro locally against their account/keys:
```
# CLI repro (run in customer's account or with their cross-account role)
aws kms decrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:alias/redwood/acme-cmk \
  --encryption-context CustomerId=acme \
  --profile customer-crossaccount
```
Also run CloudTrail lookup: 
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/NEW-KEY-ID --start-time 2026-02-28T03:00:00Z --end-time 2026-02-28T04:00:00Z
```
If that returns nothing, check the S3 bucket ACL/policy and CloudTrail delivery errors in the CloudTrail console.

cloudops_lina: I checked the org S3 bucket for CloudTrail delivery. There are PutObject failures around 03:14-03:18 UTC with error "AccessDenied" in the CloudTrail service logs. The bucket policy was updated at 03:13 UTC to add a new condition that unintentionally blocks PutObject from the CloudTrail principal when requests come from other AWS accounts. Reverting that change allowed PutObject.

kms_bot: Note: KMS audit events are only visible in CloudTrail if delivery succeeded to the trail's S3 target. If delivery is blocked at S3, you won't find the KMS Decrypt events in the trail.

support_ryan: Ok — plan: 1) tell customer to revert the S3 bucket policy change (we did that in org); 2) run the CLI repro with their role and new key alias to confirm Decrypt permissions; 3) as a short-term workaround, create a specific grant on the new CMK for the cross-account role so decrypts succeed while we re-audit the key policy.

eng_security_alex: Recommended follow-up actions: add the key-rotation checklist item to validate grants and cross-account key policy entries, and add an alert that compares API error spikes (internal telemetry) against CloudTrail event counts (if API errors spike but events missing, trigger a delivery/putobject alarm). Also audit any S3 policy changes in the org that can affect CloudTrail.

support_ryan: Will do. I'll send the repro CLI and temporary grant steps to the customer and keep this thread updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
